identity.title: A Survey of CH<SUB>3</SUB>CN and HC<SUB>3</SUB>N in Protoplanetary Disks

paper_type_evidence.quote: Based on ALMA observations of the complex nitrile species CH$_3$CN and HC$_3$N towards six protoplanetary disks, we conclude the following:

question.value: How common are CH3CN and HC3N in protoplanetary disks, what are their rotational temperatures and abundances relative to HCN, and how do these compare with comets and protostellar envelopes?

evidence.quote: A larger sample of observations is required to obtain constraints on the nitrile chemistry in disks.
as part of a line survey in disks (project code 2013.1.01070.S)

analysis_steps.goal: Disk-averaged abundance ratios relative to HCN

method.value: Use fluxes at assumed Trot of 30, 50, 70 K; H13CN to HCN with 12C/13C = 70

evidence.quote: HC$_3$N/HCN and CH$_3$CN/HCN abundance ratios are calculated for rotational temperatures of 30, 50, and 70K

evidence.quote: we assume a standard $^{12}$C/$^{13}$C ratio of 70 (with an uncertainty of 15%)

analysis_steps.goal: Parametric radial abundance modeling of V4046 Sgr and MWC 480

method.value: Power-law abundance X(r) in fixed physical disk model; RADMC-3D LTE images sampled in uv plane; emcee MCMC fit of X100 and alpha

evidence.quote: The affine-invariant MCMC package emcee (cite: Foreman-Mackey2013) was used to sample posterior distributions of both parameters $X_{100}$ and $\alpha$.

key_parameters.value: R100 = 100 AU; Rout 100 AU (V4046 Sgr), 180 AU (MWC 480); abundance reduced 1e8 above z/r=0.5; reduced 1e3 below 25 K (V4046 Sgr) or z/r<0.05 (MWC 480)

evidence.quote: molecule abundances are attenuated by a factor of 10$^{3}$ at temperatures below 25K

fitting.value: Likelihood from weighted visibility residuals; flat priors 1e-20<X100<1e-8, -3<alpha<2

evidence.quote: A flat prior was used for each parameter when generating new samples: $10^{-20}  < X_{100} <$ 10$^{-8}$ and -3 $< \alpha <$ 2.

findings_qualitative.value: HC3N detected in all disks except IM Lup; CH3CN detected in V4046 Sgr, MWC 480, HD 163296

evidence.quote: HC$_3$N is detected towards all disks except IM Lup, and CH$_3$CN is detected towards V4046 Sgr, MWC 480, and HD 163296.

findings_qualitative.value: No CH3OH detected despite strong nitrile emission, suggesting N-rich, O-poor chemistry

evidence.quote: our observations covered a number of CH$_3$OH transitions in the 5–4 ladder, with no CH$_3$OH detections despite the strong nitrile emission

claims.hypothesis: Complex nitriles are common in disks

evidence.quote: with five of six disks detected in HC$_3$N and three of six disks detected in CH$_3$CN.

claims.hypothesis: Nitrile emission arises in the temperate molecular layer

evidence.quote: Rotational temperatures derived for disks with multiple detected lines range from 29–73K

claims.hypothesis: Nitrile abundances relative to HCN are substantial at planet-forming radii
claims.experiment: Parametric abundance modeling of V4046 Sgr and MWC 480
claims.result: CH3CN/HCN a few percent, HC3N/HCN tens of percent in inner 100 AU

evidence.quote: Within 100AU, CH$_3$CN/HCN abundances are on the order of a few percent and HC$_3$N/HCN abundances on the order of tens of percent.

claims.hypothesis: Nitrile chemistry is robust across environments
claims.experiment: Compare disk ratios to comets and protostellar envelopes
claims.finding: Robust nitrile chemistry with similar outcomes

evidence.quote: although the HC$_3$N/HCN uncertainties are large due to sensitivity to the adopted rotational temperature

claims.hypothesis: UV field, age or inner cavity drive nitrile emission
claims.experiment: Compare fluxes vs L*, accretion rate, age, cavity

evidence.quote: We observe no strong trends relating these environmental properties to the nitrile emission strength.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: 29 AU cavity (mm dust hole) gives worse fit than 3 AU for V4046 Sgr

evidence.quote: An adopted 29 AU radius, corresponding to the mm dust radius hole, produces a worse fit to the data for both molecules.

limitations_admitted.value: High upper-state energy lines are insensitive to cool gas; CH3CN Trot poorly constrained due to blending; sub-thermal excitation possible
